title: Why Does the Moon Change Shape?
summary: The Moon does not really change. Find out why we see a thin curve one night and a full circle later.

steps.title: The Moon makes no light
sentences: The Moon does not make its own light.
We see it because sunlight bounces off its surface and reaches our eyes.
Half of the Moon is always lit by the Sun, just like half of Earth is always in daytime.
points: Half of it is always lit

steps.title: The Moon travels around Earth
sentences: The Moon goes around Earth once in about 29 and a half days.
As it moves, we look at its lit half from a slightly different angle each night.
That changing view is what we call the phases of the Moon.
points: Our view of the lit half changes

steps.title: The phases in order
sentences: When the Moon is between Earth and the Sun, its lit side faces away from us and we see a new moon.
A few nights later we see a thin crescent, then a half moon, then a full moon when Earth is between the Moon and the Sun.
After the full moon the lit part shrinks again until the next new moon.
points: New moon: no lit part seen

steps.title: Waxing and waning
sentences: When the lit part is growing, we say the Moon is waxing.
When it is shrinking, we say it is waning.
In India the bright part of a waxing moon is on the right side, and for a waning moon it is on the left.

facts: The same side of the Moon always faces Earth, so we never see the far side from here.
The Moon is slowly moving away from Earth, about 3.8 centimetres every year.
A full moon rises around sunset, and a new moon rises around sunrise.

quiz.q: Why can we see the Moon?
quiz.why: The Moon only reflects light from the Sun.

quiz.q: About how long is one full cycle of phases?
quiz.why: The Moon takes about 29.5 days to go from one new moon to the next.

quiz.q: When do we see a full moon?
options: When Earth is between the Moon and the Sun
When the Moon is between Earth and the Sun
quiz.why: At full moon, Earth is roughly between the Sun and the Moon, so the whole lit half faces us.
